issue_context.title: 0.12 - init fails with multiple uses of a module and module's repo contains symlink

### Expected Behavior
`terraform init` completes successfully

### Actual Behavior
`terraform init` fails with a copy error

### Steps to Reproduce

[This repo](https://github.com/rifelpet/terraform-module-relative-path-repro) contains a terraform module as well as an unrelated symlink.

When invoking the `module` module in that repo multiple times, terraform 0.12 will download the repo once and then copy it locally as many times as needed, to avoid redundant downloading. If the git repo contains a symlink (even if its not in the module's subdirectory), the copy will fail. Removing the symlink from the repo causes `init` to succeed. I'm not aware of how well terraform supports following symlinks, but in this case its not even used by terraform, it just happens to also be in the repo. It would be great if terraform's module downloading could successfully copy git repos containing symlinks.

### Additional Context
The error is logged [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/86e6481cc661b2ba694d353aab6d11838c066c7c/configs/configload/getter.go#L108) and I'm guessing that the `copyDir` function isnt looking for symlinks within the directory it is copying, causing [this](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/86e6481cc661b2ba694d353aab6d11838c066c7c/configs/configload/copy_dir.go#L63) open to fail.

review_comments:
I'm a little unclear on the control flow here... after we've made this directory, does `filepath.Walk` then visit the contents of the directory that the symlink refers to? If it doesn't, then wouldn't we just end up with an empty directory here?

I wonder if we need to recursively call `copyDir` here to also copy the _contents_ of the directory, rather than just making the directory.

I must admit I copied this logic from the preceding section (`if info.IsDir() {`). I _thought_ that was the behavior, but on closer inspection that doesn't seem to be the case. I will keep poking at it and extend the test coverage to include a symlinked module, too.
